text:
maria: Hey all — saw a sharp 600ms p95 jump on a few hosts during the midnight deploy window, traced to KV cache churn. Figured I'd dump notes here: https://ci.internal/perf/2150/wf
chen: ugh. which eviction policy were those hosts on?
maria: Those Dedicated lanes were on LRU with default reuse_window=2s and paging watermark at 78%.
alex: Any repro traces? pprof or flame graphs?
maria: Uploaded a short profile: `s3://perf-artifacts/kv-churn/2150001123/profile.pb.gz`. Immediate symptom: CPU spike in kv_evict_loop + outbound copy, then many short-lived allocations.
jamal: Can you paste the top lines from `go tool pprof -top`?
maria: Sure — pasted excerpt:

```
23.7%  kv_evict_loop
15.2%  kv_page_and_move
12.8%  memcpy
9.5%   handle_request (store_kv)
6.1%   mutex_lock
```

maria: Also saw lots of `reinsert` logs like `reinserted key=abcd len=4096 ttl=0` which suggests reuse-window collisions.
chen: Hmm. LRU + reuse_window small -> hot items being evicted then immediately reinserted by concurrent long-context requests.
alex: Did batching heuristics change? If more long seqs are batched, reuse pattern gets worse.
maria: Yes, we backported microbatching change on 2025-11-10 increasing max_seq_batch to 8 for throughput. Correlated with first regressions.
jamal: Two quick experiments to run:
1) Flip policy to FIFO on a canary node (same load) and compare p95.
2) Increase reuse_window to 10s and see if reinserts drop.
chen: I'll run (1) now on node pool `dedicated-a` with A/B pinning.
sre-bot: deploy started: canary pool dedicated-a -> set config `eviction_policy=FIFO` (id: dply-2150-1)
chen: Canary is live. Initial telemetry looks promising: evict churn down ~40% in 5m.
alex: Interesting — FIFO reduces reinserts because old entries stick around even if not LRU-favored by concurrent tails.
maria: But FIFO increases external fragmentation in long contexts — saw some free slab gaps. Memory variance + paging threshold crossing caused a waterfall where pager freed noncontiguous chunks causing compaction pressure.
jamal: Do you have logs showing pager activity?
maria: Paste:

```
[2025-11-11T00:12:34Z] pager: free_chunk at 0x7f13 len=65536
[2025-11-11T00:12:34Z] pager: mark_used at 0x7f22 len=16
[2025-11-11T00:12:35Z] pager: reclaim_loop triggered watermark=0.82
```

maria: Then a brief latency step until the pager finished compaction.
chen: So FIFO reduced quick reinserts but worsened fragmentation -> longer tail during compaction.
alex: Kernel selection might mediate this: memcpy-heavy hotspots suggest we're moving KV payloads a lot. If we switch to a kernel with in-place reference-counting support that avoids copies for same-device transfers, the memcpy percentage could drop.
jamal: Good call. We have a no-copy kernel prototype: `kref-v2`. Can we test it on the FIFO canary to see combined effect?
maria: Yes, can run kref-v2 on a single host and run load. I'll queue it.
sre-bot: deploy started: host dedicated-a-03 -> runtime-kernel=kref-v2 (id: dply-2150-2)
chen: After kref-v2 landed: memcpy top went from 12.8% to 3.4%, CPU p95 down 30%. Latency tail still has spikes but slightly smaller.
alex: That implies two orthogonal issues: eviction policy influences reuse churn; kernel reduces move overhead. We still need to address fragmentation.
jamal: For fragmentation, ideas:
- implement slab coalescing on free interval detection
- tune pager watermarks (increase high watermark to 0.9 for FIFO only)
- prefer LRU for pools dominated by short contexts and FIFO for long-context-heavy pools
maria: Also tracked request patterns: long-context sessions (~>8k tokens) cause large KV spans that, when evicted, leave uneven holes. We could pin large KV entries to a separate arena to avoid hurting small-item locality.
chen: I'll prototype a split-arena approach: small-value arena vs large-value arena threshold = 16KB. Put it behind feature flag.
jamal: Quick A/B: set `high_watermark=0.9` and `large_value_threshold=16384` on a second canary pool and compare.
maria: Running that now. Preliminary: reinserts down another 12%, fragmentation metric (free-chunk-count variance) drops ~25%.
alex: Nice. Any correctness concerns switching between LRU and FIFO? We saw a small repro where LRU had an ordering race with concurrent reuse leading to double-free log entry.
chen: Right — found a race: in evict path we checked `if refcount == 0` then `remove_and_free`, but a concurrent reinsert could increment refcount after the check and before free. Added atomic compare-and-swap to avoid.
jamal: Patch landed in runtime: `evict: use atomic transition from 0 -> reserved before free` (PR #4891).
maria: After that fix, one rare double-free repro does not reproduce locally. Will monitor canaries for a few hours.
sre-bot: monitoring: canary pools d-2150-1 and d-2150-2 OK for 35m; slight tail at 2am connected to GC runs.
chen: Summary proposals from thread:
- short-term: switch FIFO on long-context pools + kref-v2 where available
- medium-term: split arenas for large KV values + increase high_watermark for FIFO
- correctness: keep atomic refcount fix (PR #4891)
- further: consider telemetry to auto-route pools by median seq_len
maria: Great summary. I'll open a doc with runbooks and links to artifacts. Thanks team :clap:
alex: can you add a small test harness that simulates interleaved long-tail reinsert pattern? would be useful for regression tests.
maria: Yep, will add to perf-suite (task id: PERF-872)
jamal: tagging product in case any SLA customers hit related regression.
maria: ping @product-eng — fyi, this is infra-only, no API change, but potentially affects latency intermittently for Dedicated customers.
